newsitem.title: USA: Utah group to sue Clinton for creating monument.
newsitem.headline: Utah group to sue Clinton for creating monument.

text.p: The Utah Association of Counties plans to file a lawsuit Monday to void the creation of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, an aide to Utah Republican Rep. Christopher Cannon said Friday.
The 1.7 million acre scenic redrock area in southern Utah has potential coal and oil deposits.
President Clinton designated the new national monument at the height of the political campaign season last year, drawing cheers from the environmental community and objections from mining advocates.

The Utah group plans to file the lawsuit in a U.S. district court in Utah on the grounds that the monument "goes beyond the scope for which it was intended, and the president does not have the power to close off mining on the land," Cannon's spokesman Peter Valcarce said.
The counties group plans to hold a news conference in Washington to announce the lawsuit Monday, with the support of Utah Republicans Sen. Orrin Hatch, Rep. James Hansen, and Cannon.

Saying that Clinton had abused his privilege to name a monument simply for political gain, Hatch pushed a bill that would require congressional approval for a proclamation involving more than 5,000 acres.
